q: A colleague accidentally changed part of a shared Doc. Which feature can help inspect and restore earlier content?
exp: Version history records prior versions and edits.

q: Which feature is best for leaving targeted feedback on one sentence in a student's Doc?
exp: Comments can be anchored to specific text.

q: Which two features are especially useful for collaborative feedback in Docs? (Select two.)
exp: Comments and suggestions support review without requiring silent overwrites.

q: A team wants to avoid emailing different versions of a presentation back and forth. What should they do?
choices: Share one Slides file with appropriate access
Export a new PDF after every edit
exp: A shared cloud file gives collaborators one current version.

q: Which setup best supports real-time collaborative writing by a student group?
choices: Share one Doc with edit access to group members
exp: A shared editable Doc supports simultaneous contributions.

q: Students are peer-reviewing essays. Which workflow best preserves the author's control while enabling feedback?
exp: Commenter access enables feedback without giving peers full control.

q: A teacher wants students to reflect on what they learned after a project. Which approach is most structured?
choices: Use a Form with reflection prompts
exp: A Form can gather consistent reflection responses.

q: A project team wants to know who changed a shared file and when. Which feature should they inspect?
exp: Version history identifies edits and editors over time.

q: What is a benefit of using comments with @mentions in a shared document?
choices: You can direct feedback or action to a specific collaborator
It changes all viewers to editors
exp: @mentions help target feedback to a specific collaborator.

q: Students are jointly collecting research notes. Which choice best prevents duplicated versions?
choices: Use one shared Doc or Sheet with appropriate permissions
Ask each student to email separate copies repeatedly
Use a read-only PDF for note entry
exp: A shared file keeps contributions in one current workspace.

q: Which two practices support productive group collaboration? (Select two.)
choices: Use shared files with appropriate access
Give everyone ownership of every file
exp: Clear responsibilities and sensible sharing reduce confusion.

q: A teacher wants to discuss and resolve feedback in a shared Doc. What workflow fits best?
choices: Use comments, replies, and Resolve when addressed
Use only file names for feedback
exp: Comment threads support discussion and can be resolved when complete.

q: A student needs to suggest wording changes while allowing the teacher to accept or reject them. Which mode is best?
exp: Suggestion mode lets the owner accept or reject proposed edits.

q: Which option best supports a group brainstorming activity where everyone needs to contribute text at the same time?
choices: A Gmail draft visible to one person
exp: A shared editable Doc supports simultaneous input.

q: A teacher wants a record of discussion around a specific slide element. Which approach is best?
choices: Add comments on the Slides file
exp: Comments keep discussion attached to the relevant collaborative artifact.

q: Which action is most appropriate after a collaborator has addressed a comment in a Doc?
exp: Resolving a comment marks the feedback thread as addressed.
